name: container-query
summary: A @container rule, taking the same argument shapes as breakpoint so the two read alike. Sizes may be a key from $map-for-breakpoints or a raw length, and a length is the common case because a container is usually narrower than the viewport. Nothing matches at all unless an ancestor was declared with the container mixin.

arguments.name: $params
accepts: a size, for exactly that width, which prints a warning: write only instead
one of min, max, only or between followed by a size; max with a key ends before it

a size is a key from $map-for-breakpoints, or a length in any unit a width condition takes, 0 or a calculation; a percentage, a bare number, another unit and a word that is not a key are refused, because the query would never match
$name as a keyword, to query one named container

caveats: A size on its own matches exactly that width, `(width: 400px)`, which is a single pixel, and the mixin prints a warning. Write `only` for that width, or `min`, `max` or a range for anything wider.

A range that ends at a key from $map-for-breakpoints, and `max` with a key, end before the key in range syntax: `container-query(max, medium)` is `(width < 768px)` and `container-query(small, medium)` is `(min-width: 576px) and (width < 768px)`. So neighbouring ranges do not both apply at the key. A length written by hand is used as written, so `max, 399px` stays `(max-width: 399px)`, and a zero key is left alone. Until 4.0.0 both ended on the key and overlapped there.
